text: This lesson wraps up FeedbackScope and turns it into a real portfolio piece -- not just a project that runs, but one you can explain.

Lesson 23 gave it a multi-stage Dockerfile, one instance, and defaults. Lesson 24 added concurrency-based autoscaling, a health check that actually exercises the model, and a deliberate decision to skip caching. The result: every configuration choice has a stated reason.

"I built a sentiment API and deployed it" is a weak answer. "I scaled on concurrency instead of CPU because that's what reflected real load, and skipped caching because the traffic pattern didn't justify it" is a strong one -- it shows decisions, not just steps.

The README should cover what the service does with a real example, the Dockerfile and why it's built that way, the autoscaling policy with its justification, and what you'd add next with more time or budget. The reasoning is the actual portfolio piece.

This course closes out the infrastructure side of the AI Engineer path -- your app can now run somewhere, survive a release, and scale. Next up: AI Security, Evaluation & Monitoring, picking up exactly where a deployed service's real risks start.
